newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: JUSTIN DOWNGRADED BUT GETTING CLOSER
Tropical Cyclone Justin has lost some of its intensity overnight, but has moved closer to the Queensland coast.
It has been downgraded from a category three to a category two cyclone, and is about 760 kilometres east northeast of Cooktown and 810 kilometres north northeast of Bowen.
It's moving southwest at 15 kilometres an hour.
A Tropical Cyclone Watch is current for coastal and island communities between Cooktown and Mackay.
ORION TO JOIN SEARCH FOR MISSING YACHT NEAR JUSTIN
An Orion aircraft has left the Air Force base at Edinburgh, north of Adelaide, to take over search duties for a yacht missing in the Coral Sea, north-east of Townsville.
A distress beacon was activated by the crew of the Queen Charlotte, which is believed to have been about 100-kilometres from the eye of Cyclone Justin.
Five people are aboard the New Zealand registered schooner.
Sea and weather conditions in the area are said to have been severe, with six metre wind-driven waves on top of a swell of five metres.
The P-3C Orion from Adelaide will take over from an airforce Hercules.
PORT MORESBY QUIET THIS MORNING
Port Moreseby is quiet this morning with Murray Barracks, the main military centre and focus of the protest, showing no outward signs of disturbance.
But PNG is facing another day of higher political tension as the standoff between military and political leaders continues.
After three days of confrontation, the Prime Minister, Sir Julius Chan, yesterday gave some ground to his rebellious military by indicating he would end his use of mercenaries.
But it's not clear if his actions will be enough to resolve the crisis threatening his government.
Yesterday, the soldiers in the barracks were openly defying the authority of Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan.
Meanwhile, some Sandline International Mercenaries, hired to train Papua New Guinea defence personell and to fight in Bougainville, have left the country saying their contract has been cancelled.
JERVIS BAY COMMUNITY CELEBRATING NO NUKE DECISION
The Jervis Bay community is celebrating today after assurances from the Federal Government that a nuclear reactor won't be placed in the area.

Although the Government said it was never on the agenda, the Opposition yesterday used question time to table a leaked document that showed Jervis Bay as an option for the re-siting of the Lucas Heights nuclear reactor.
Federal Science Minister Peter McGauran has now officially ruled it out.
Federal MP Steve Dargavel, whose electorate takes in the newly named Budaree National Park, at Jervis Bay, says he's relieved.
CHIEF JUSTICE SAYS PEOPLE SHOULD BE THE SAME-MARRIED OR NOT

The Chief Justice of the Family Court says he can't see why the property of couples living in de facto relationships, shouldn't be dealt with according to the same principles applied to married couples.
Justice Alastair Nicholson was speaking at a conference on the future of families hosted by Brisbane's Griffith University.
He told delegates people are entitled to the same rights regardless of whether or not they're married, and said he didn't exclude same sex relationships.
Justice Nicholson also spoke about the introduction of handover centres.
He said handover centres are in the interests of children at the centre of custody battles, because they help neutralise the animosity between seperated parents.
CENTURY ARBITRATION BEGINS TODAY
The Managing Director of the Century Zinc project in Queensland's Gulf Country, says the arbitration process, which gets underway today, is regrettable but necessary.
The Native Title Tribunal will hold a direction hearing in Brisbane to determine what evidence must be presented before it decides whether to grant mining leases to Century Zinc.
This follows refusal by six of 12 native title claimants to sign a deal proposed by the company and the State Government.
Ian Williams has told ABC Radio, the company hopes to achieve a positive determination, allowing the government to issue the mining and other leases it needs to get on with the project.
THIRD NIGHT OF DEBATE ON ANTI-EUTHANASIA BILL
The Kevin Andrews anti-euthanasia bill, which aims to override the Northern Territory's voluntary euthanasia law has been described as outrageous during Senate debate.
Last night was the third night of debate in the Upper House on the bill, and so far 42 Senators have had their say on the matter.
Democrats Senator Vicki Bourne spoke against the Bill saying its an outrageous step to take to override a piece of Northern Territory Legislation.
Her comments were supported by Territory Senator Grant Tambling who described the bill as short-sighted, paternalistic and patronising in the extreme.
Their opinions, however, are in the minority with 25 senators so far, giving their support to the Andrews bill.
